Hasnain, Han & Economo (2025) on the MAP dataset, DANDI:000363¶

Paper: Hasnain M. A., Han Y. & Economo M. N., "Mapping neural subspace dynamics onto the structure of the mouse descending motor system", bioRxiv doi:10.1101/2025.10.17.682917 (preprint version 1). The claims file claims/hasnain-2025.yaml was written from the preprint's full text (PMC12632980); it fixes what is tested.

Dataset: DANDI:000363 (Mesoscale Activity Map Dataset, Chen et al. 2024), version 0.231012.2129, streamed from the archive. The paper cites the dandiset without a version ("https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/000363"), so the most recent published version is pinned. The earlier versions hold the same 174 sessions; the versions before 0.231012.2129 total 19 to 67 GB and this one 65.7 TB, as it adds the raw recordings. The cell "Version check" compares the units of one session between this version and 0.230822.0128.

The paper reuses the MAP data for Figure 4 only. Its own recordings (Figures 1 to 3, Extended Data Figures 2 and 3) are not public, so those eleven claims are blocked.

Claim Tested here
own-recordings-cohort, fig1i-selectivity-proportions, fig2c-subspace-variance, fig2e-potent-only-units, fig2f-letn-preference-like-un, fig2gh-letn-span-subspaces, ed2f-false-negatives, fig3c-network-beats-linear, fig3d-letn-un-movement-encoding, ed3-letn-fast-switch, ed3a-cd-early-un-not-letn Blocked: the paper's own recordings are not public

A second notebook, reproduce_hasnain_2025_g2.ipynb, repeats the tests on the ALM and medulla sessions under reading G2 of the unit selection (unit_quality good, CCF labels transferred from the nearest unit classified good); this notebook uses G1 (classification good) throughout.

The methods are those of the claims file (header items M1 to M10, which cite the paper) and, where it lacks a detail, the paper's Methods; the helper map_subspace.py says where each parameter comes from.

import os
os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "2")
import collections
import resource
import time
import zlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

import map_subspace as ms

T0 = time.time()
KEY = "hasnain-2025"


def seed(claim, k=0):
    return zlib.crc32(f"{KEY}/{claim}".encode()) + k


SEED_OFFSETS = [0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000]
pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 30)

Data check¶

Every file's units table is read (probe target from the electrodes' location, classification, unit_quality, anno_name), then the sessions are selected as in M1 and M2.

In [2]:

tables = ms.survey(assets)

print("classification x unit_quality:", dict(cls_q))
anno_by_cls = collections.Counter((c, a != "") for t in tables.values() for c, a in zip(t["classification"], t["anno"]))

from dandi.dandiapi import DandiAPIClient

old = DandiAPIClient().get_dandiset(ms.DANDISET_ID, "0.230822.0128")
old_paths = {a.path: a for a in old.get_assets()}
ses_key = lambda p: p.split("_behavior")[0]
old_by_ses = {ses_key(p): a for p, a in old_paths.items()}
print("assets in 0.230822.0128:", len(old_paths), " same paths as pinned:", len(set(old_paths) & set(tables)),
      " same sessions:", len(set(old_by_ses) & {ses_key(p) for p in tables}))
print("example path there:", next(p for p in old_paths if ses_key(p) == ses_key(probe_path)))
cmp = {}
for label, url in [("0.231012.2129", dict(assets)[probe_path]),
                   ("0.230822.0128", old_by_ses[ses_key(probe_path)].get_content_url(follow_redirects=1, strip_query=True))]:
    f = ms.open_file(url)
    u = f["units"]
    cmp[label] = dict(units=u["id"].shape[0], spikes=u["spike_times"].shape[0],
                      good=int(sum(np.array(ms._dec(u["classification"][:])) == "good")),
                      first_spikes=np.round(u["spike_times"][:5], 6).tolist(),
                      acquisition=sorted(f["acquisition"].keys()))
print(pd.DataFrame(cmp).T)

Selection (M1, M2)¶

Reading G1: units classified 'good' (classification), with a CCF label of MOs on a probe described as targeting ALM, or a label of IRN, GRN or PARN. anno_name is filled only for units classified good. The electrodes table gives the CCF coordinates (x, y, z) of each electrode, so the other readings (G2, unit_quality good; U2, all units) are formed by giving each unit the label of the nearest unit classified good on the same probe, within 20 um (an assumption; the cell of map-session-selection checks it and gives the counts).

Trials, movement and clocks¶

For each selected session: the trials kept (hit or miss, no photostimulation, no early lick, and a sample cue 1.85 s before the go cue, the paper's 1.2 s delay; the trial labels and the trials left out for another delay are printed), the go cue inside each trial, the jaw and nose speed and the movement threshold. Clock checks: the tongue becomes visible to the side camera, and the first lick is logged, shortly after the go cue (behaviour clock against trial table); and lick direction is decoded from the selected units' spike counts in 200 ms windows around the go cue, against the same decoder with the trial labels shuffled (spike clock against trial table).

In [5]:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score

urls = dict(assets)
W = ms.WINDOWS["W1"]
sessions = {}
check_rows = []
labels_seen = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
rng_check = np.random.default_rng(seed("map-session-selection"))
for p in list(alm_med) + list(bilateral):
    if p in sessions:
        continue
    regions = alm_med[p] if p in alm_med else bilateral[p]
    ids = sorted(set(sum((v for k, v in regions.items() if k != "alm_sides"), [])))
    s = ms.load_session(urls[p], ids)
    for k in ("outcome", "photostim_duration", "early_lick", "trial_instruction"):
        labels_seen[k].update(s["trials"][k])
    gos = ms.go_times(s)
    keep = ms.trial_mask(s)
    go = gos[keep]
    onset_all = ms.sample_onset(s, gos)
    other_delay = (np.isin(np.array(s["trials"]["outcome"]), ["hit", "miss"]) & (np.array(s["trials"]["photostim_duration"]) == "N/A")
                   & (np.array(s["trials"]["early_lick"]) == "no early") & np.isfinite(gos) & ~(np.abs(onset_all - ms.SAMPLE_ONSET) < 0.02))
    sample_rel = onset_all[keep]
    speed = ms.speed_bins(s, go, W)
    finite = speed[np.isfinite(speed) & (speed > 0)]
    log_thr = ms.otsu_threshold(np.log10(finite))
    # tongue visibility and first lick
    f = ms.open_file(urls[p])
    tg = f["acquisition/BehavioralTimeSeries/Camera0_side_TongueTracking"]
    tts, tlik = tg["timestamps"][:], tg["data"][:, 2]
    licks = np.sort(np.r_[f["acquisition/BehavioralEvents/left_lick_times/timestamps"][:],
                          f["acquisition/BehavioralEvents/right_lick_times/timestamps"][:]])
    hit = np.array(s["trials"]["outcome"])[keep] == "hit"
    tongue_lat, lick_lat, tongue_pre = [], [], []
    for g in go[hit]:
        lo, hi = np.searchsorted(tts, [g, g + 1.0])
        k = np.where(tlik[lo:hi] > 0.9)[0]
        tongue_lat.append(tts[lo + k[0]] - g if len(k) else np.nan)
        lo2, hi2 = np.searchsorted(tts, [g - 0.5, g])
        tongue_pre.append(np.mean(tlik[lo2:hi2] > 0.9) if hi2 > lo2 else np.nan)
        j = np.searchsorted(licks, g)
        lick_lat.append(licks[j] - g if j < len(licks) else np.nan)
    # decoding lick direction from spike counts
    right = np.array(s["trials"]["trial_instruction"])[keep] == "right"
    acc = {}
    for w0 in (-2.0, -1.0, -0.4, 0.2, 0.8):
        X = np.stack([np.diff(np.searchsorted(s["spikes"][i], np.c_[go + w0, go + w0 + 0.2]), axis=1)[:, 0]
                      for i in ids], axis=1)
        clf = LogisticRegression(C=0.1, max_iter=2000)
        acc[w0] = cross_val_score(clf, X, right, cv=5).mean()
        acc[f"{w0} shuffled"] = cross_val_score(clf, X, rng_check.permutation(right), cv=5).mean()
    sessions[p] = dict(sess=s, keep=keep, go=go, speed=speed, log_thr=log_thr, regions=regions)
    check_rows.append(dict(session=p.split("/")[1][:30], trials=len(keep), kept=int(keep.sum()),
                           hits=int(hit.sum()), right=int(right.sum()),
                           go_in_trial=int(np.isfinite(gos).sum()),
                           speed_thr=round(10 ** log_thr, 1),
                           tongue_lat_ms=round(1000 * np.nanmedian(tongue_lat)),
                           tongue_pre_go=round(np.nanmean(tongue_pre), 3),
                           lick_lat_ms=round(1000 * np.nanmedian(lick_lat)),
                           other_delay=int(other_delay.sum()),
                           other_delay_onsets=",".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x, _ in collections.Counter(np.round(onset_all[other_delay], 2)).most_common(2)),
                           sample_from_go_s=round(float(np.nanmedian(sample_rel)), 3),
                           sample_min=round(float(np.nanmin(sample_rel)), 3), sample_max=round(float(np.nanmax(sample_rel)), 3),
                           **{f"acc {k}": round(v, 2) for k, v in acc.items()}))
    del f
checks = pd.DataFrame(check_rows)
print(checks.to_string())
print("trials kept per session: %d to %d" % (checks.kept.min(), checks.kept.max()))
print("trial labels over the selected sessions:", {k: dict(v) for k, v in labels_seen.items()})
print("correct and error trials left out for a sample onset other than -1.85 s (other delay): %d to %d per session, %d in all"
      % (checks.other_delay.min(), checks.other_delay.max(), checks.other_delay.sum()))
print("sample cue onset relative to the go cue in the kept trials: %.3f to %.3f s"
      % (checks.sample_min.min(), checks.sample_max.max()))
print("baseline window", ms.BASELINE, "s: ends no later than the earliest sample onset of a kept trial:",
      ms.BASELINE[1] <= checks.sample_min.min() + 1e-9)
print("median tongue latency over sessions: %d ms; first lick %d ms" % (checks.tongue_lat_ms.median(), checks.lick_lat_ms.median()))
print("elapsed %.0f s" % (time.time() - T0))

Claim map-session-selection¶

In the MAP dataset, the paper's selection gives 20 bilateral ALM sessions from 10 mice (961 right and 1055 left ALM units) and ALM and medulla sessions with 604 ALM units and 724 medullary reticular nucleus units.

Criterion: session counts match S1 (16) or S2 (11) for ALM and medulla and 20 bilateral, and every unit count within tolerance under one reading of M2. U1 (good units in the regions) is the main reading. Only units classified good carry a CCF label, so for U2 (all units in those regions), as for G2, each other unit takes the label of the nearest unit classified good on the same probe, within 20 um (an assumption); the counts of all units on each region's probe are also shown.

# label transfer for readings G2 and U2: among units classified good, does the nearest other such
# unit on the same probe (electrode CCF coordinates) carry the same CCF label?
agree = n_lab = 0
for t in tables.values():
    xyz, an = np.asarray(t["xyz"], float), np.array(t["anno"], dtype=object)
    g, tgs = np.array(t["classification"]) == "good", np.array(t["target"])
    for tg in set(tgs):
        lab = np.where(g & (tgs == tg) & np.isfinite(xyz).all(1))[0]
        if len(lab) < 2:
            continue
        d = np.linalg.norm(xyz[lab][:, None] - xyz[lab][None], axis=2)
        np.fill_diagonal(d, np.inf)
        agree += int((an[lab][d.argmin(1)] == an[lab]).sum())
        n_lab += len(lab)
print(f"nearest unit classified good has the same CCF label: {agree} of {n_lab} ({100 * agree / n_lab:.1f}%)")

Result: not reproduced. With the dataset's CCF labels and units classified good (G1), the paper's rule gives 17 bilateral ALM sessions from 9 mice (paper 20 from 10) and 5 ALM and medulla sessions from 4 mice (paper 16, or 11 from 7). The left ALM count (1001) is within tolerance of 1055; the right ALM count (858 against 961), the ALM count of the ALM and medulla sessions (300 against 604) and the medulla count (340 against 724) are not. Among units classified good, the nearest other such unit on the probe carries the same CCF label for 97.3%, so the other readings were formed by that transfer. With unit_quality good (G2, within 20 um) the rule gives 31 bilateral sessions from 12 mice (2767 and 2830 units) and 19 ALM and medulla sessions from 7 mice (1501 ALM and 1745 medulla units); within 0 um 28 and 13 sessions, within 40 um 35 and 22; with all units (U2) 44 and 28. No reading gives the session counts together with the unit counts. G1 stays the main reading: its bilateral unit counts are near the paper's, where G2's are 2.7 to 2.9 times them, and "classified as 'good'" names the classification column. With a threshold of 20 good units the G1 ALM and medulla sessions number 14, with 25 they number 9.

Per-region subspaces, ALM and medulla sessions¶

For each ALM and medulla session and region: z-scored rates, the movement mask, the dimensions from the shuffle, and the subspaces. The main reading is W1, B1, D1 and the baseline z-score; the readings W2, B2, D2 and the z-score of example.m are each run with the others held at the main reading. The subspace generator uses the seed of fig4c-alm-null-potent-similar, the first claim that uses it.

In [8]:
READINGS = {"main": dict(W="W1", B="B1", D="D1", Z="baseline"),
            "W2": dict(W="W2", B="B1", D="D1", Z="baseline"),
            "B2": dict(W="W1", B="B2", D="D1", Z="baseline"),
            "D2": dict(W="W1", B="B1", D="D2", Z="baseline"),
            "Zall": dict(W="W1", B="B1", D="D1", Z="all")}


def prepare(p, region_ids, reading, store=None):
    v = (sessions if store is None else store)[p]
    s, go = v["sess"], v["go"]
    win = ms.WINDOWS[reading["W"]]
    r = ms.rates([s["spikes"][i] for i in region_ids], go, ms.WINDOWS["W1"])
    off = int(round((win[0] - ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0]) / ms.BIN))
    r = r[:, off:]
    if reading["Z"] == "baseline":
        # the baseline lies before W2's start, so it is always taken from the W1 rates
        rw1 = ms.rates([s["spikes"][i] for i in region_ids], go, ms.WINDOWS["W1"]) if off else r
        b0 = int(round((ms.BASELINE[0] - ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0]) / ms.BIN))
        b1 = int(round((ms.BASELINE[1] - ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0]) / ms.BIN))
        base = rw1[:, b0:b1].reshape(-1, r.shape[2])
        mu, sd = base.mean(0), base.std(0)
        allsd = r.reshape(-1, r.shape[2]).std(0)
        nfb = int((sd <= 1e-9).sum())
        sd = np.where(sd <= 1e-9, np.where(allsd > 0, allsd, 1.0), sd)
        z = ((r - mu) / sd).astype(np.float32)
    else:
        z, nfb = ms.zscore(r, win, mode="all")
    mv = ms.movement_mask(v["speed"][:, off:], v["log_thr"], short_runs_move=reading["B"] == "B2")
    return z, mv, nfb


fits = {}        # (session, region, reading) -> fit
fit_rows = []
rng_sub = np.random.default_rng(seed("fig4c-alm-null-potent-similar"))
for p, s in alm_med.items():
    for reg in ("ALM", "medulla"):
        dims_main = None
        for rname, rd in READINGS.items():
            z, mv, nfb = prepare(p, s[reg], rd)
            dims = fits[(p, reg, "main")]["d_raw"] if rname == "D2" else None
            fit = ms.fit_region(z, mv, rng_sub, dim_mode=rd["D"], dims=dims)
            fit["n_fallback"] = nfb
            fit["moving_frac"] = float((mv == 1).sum() / (mv >= 0).sum())
            fit["proj"] = (z @ fit["qn"]).astype(np.float32)
            if rname == "main":
                fit["z"] = z
                fit["mv"] = mv
            fits[(p, reg, rname)] = fit
            ve = ms.ve_readings(fit)
            fit_rows.append(dict(session=p.split("/")[1][:30], region=reg, reading=rname, units=z.shape[2],
                                 d_null=fit["d"][0], d_pot=fit["d"][1], d_null_raw=fit["d_raw"][0],
                                 d_pot_raw=fit["d_raw"][1], moving=round(fit["moving_frac"], 3),
                                 fallback=nfb, z_absmax=float(np.abs(z).max()),
                                 **{f"{k} {n}": 100 * x for k, vv in ve.items() for n, x in zip(("null", "pot", "both"), vv)}))
    print(p.split("/")[1][:30], "done, elapsed %.0f s" % (time.time() - T0))
fit_df = pd.DataFrame(fit_rows)
print(fit_df.round(1).to_string())
print("peak memory %.0f MB" % (resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1e3))

# moving bins by epoch (share of tracked bins), readings B1 and B2, and bins without tracking
tax_w1 = ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0] + ms.BIN * np.arange(fits[(next(iter(alm_med)), "ALM", "main")]["mv"].shape[1])
ep_spans = {"baseline": ms.BASELINE, "sample": (-1.8, -1.2), "delay": (-1.2, 0.0), "response": (0.0, 1.5)}
mrows = []
for p in alm_med:
    for B in ("B1", "B2"):
        mv = ms.movement_mask(sessions[p]["speed"], sessions[p]["log_thr"], short_runs_move=B == "B2")
        row = dict(session=p.split("/")[1][:30], reading=B, untracked=round(float((mv < 0).mean()), 3))
        for ep, (a, b) in ep_spans.items():
            m = mv[:, (tax_w1 >= a) & (tax_w1 < b)]
            row[ep] = round(float((m == 1).sum() / max((m >= 0).sum(), 1)), 3)
        mrows.append(row)
print(pd.DataFrame(mrows).to_string())

Claim fig4b-medulla-selectivity¶

Medullary reticular nucleus units are selective for lick direction in each epoch, most in the response epoch (sample 7%, delay 21%, response 49% of 724 units).

Correct trials only, equal random samples of right and left trials (the smaller count; M7), AUROC in each of the five epochs, 1000 label shuffles. Readings E1 (a unit counts for an epoch if selective in either sub-epoch) and E2 (each sub-epoch alone); Bonferroni (p < 0.01) and uncorrected (p < 0.05). Firing rates are the smoothed 5 ms rates (not z-scored) averaged over the epoch's bins.

In [9]:
def selectivity(rng, block_trials=None):
    out = []
    for p, s in alm_med.items():
        v = sessions[p]
        trials = v["sess"]["trials"]
        out_arr = np.array(trials["outcome"])[v["keep"]]
        instr = np.array(trials["trial_instruction"])[v["keep"]]
        r_idx = np.where((out_arr == "hit") & (instr == "right"))[0]
        l_idx = np.where((out_arr == "hit") & (instr == "left"))[0]
        n = min(len(r_idx), len(l_idx))
        pick = np.r_[rng.choice(r_idx, n, replace=False), rng.choice(l_idx, n, replace=False)]
        is_right = np.r_[np.ones(n, bool), np.zeros(n, bool)]
        blocks = None if block_trials is None else pick // block_trials
        r = ms.rates([v["sess"]["spikes"][i] for i in s["medulla"]], v["go"][pick], ms.WINDOWS["W1"])
        tax = ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0] + ms.BIN * np.arange(r.shape[1])
        for j in range(r.shape[2]):
            row = dict(session=p.split("/")[1][:30], unit=s["medulla"][j], n_per_side=n)
            for ep, (a, b) in ms.EPOCHS.items():
                x = r[:, (tax >= a) & (tax < b), j].mean(1)
                auc, pv = ms.selectivity_p(x, is_right, rng, blocks=blocks)
                row[ep] = pv
                row[ep + "_auc"] = auc
            out.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


def summarize_sel(df, alpha):
    sig = {ep: df[ep] < alpha for ep in ms.EPOCHS}
    e1 = {"sample": sig["sample"], "delay": sig["early_delay"] | sig["late_delay"],
          "response": sig["early_response"] | sig["late_response"]}
    res = {f"E1 {k}": 100 * v.mean() for k, v in e1.items()}
    res.update({f"E2 {k}": 100 * v.mean() for k, v in sig.items()})
    return res

pos_rows = []
for p in alm_med:
    v = sessions[p]
    out_arr = np.array(v["sess"]["trials"]["outcome"])[v["keep"]]

print(pd.DataFrame(pos_rows).to_string())

print("labels shuffled within blocks of 30 kept trials (claim seed plus 1):")
print(pd.Series(summarize_sel(sel_block, 0.01)).round(1).to_string())

Result: partially reproduced. Of 340 medulla units (G1), under E1 with the Bonferroni threshold 32.4% are selective in the sample epoch, 49.1% in the delay epoch and 85.9% in the response epoch (paper 7, 21 and 49%). Under E1 the order holds (response highest, sample lowest) for every seed and both thresholds; under E2 the early delay sub-epoch (30.3%) falls below the sample epoch (32.4%). No reading brings a value within tolerance: the E2 sub-epochs give 30.3 to 66.8%, and the uncorrected threshold higher values. Over the five seeds the E1 Bonferroni values range from 30.9 to 32.9% (sample), 47.9 to 51.5% (delay) and 85.0 to 85.9% (response). By session the sample value runs from 1.7 to 54.8%. The share of right trials changes over the session (0.13 to 0.73 by fifth in one session), but slow drift does not explain the high values: with labels shuffled only within blocks of 30 trials they are 30.3, 47.9 and 85.9%. Under reading G2 (second notebook, 1745 units) they are 16.7, 28.3 and 63.4%, also outside tolerance, with the same order. The units differ from the paper's (340 where the paper has 724).

Claims fig4c-alm-null-potent-similar and fig4c-medulla-null-smaller¶

Variance explained per session (M6) under V1, V2 and V3, for each reading of M3 to M5; paired two-sided t test of null against potent over the ALM and medulla sessions.

seed_rows = []
for rname in ("main", "B2"):
    for k in SEED_OFFSETS:
        rng_k = np.random.default_rng(seed("fig4c-alm-null-potent-similar", k))
        for p, s in alm_med.items():
            for reg in ("ALM", "medulla"):
                f0 = fits[(p, reg, "main")]
                if k == 0:
                    fit = fits[(p, reg, rname)]
                else:
                    mv = f0["mv"] if rname == "main" else ms.movement_mask(sessions[p]["speed"], sessions[p]["log_thr"], short_runs_move=True)
                    fit = ms.fit_region(f0["z"], mv, rng_k)
                ve = ms.ve_readings(fit)
                seed_rows.append(dict(reading=rname, offset=k, session=p, region=reg, d_null=fit["d"][0], d_pot=fit["d"][1],
                                      d_null_raw=fit["d_raw"][0],
                                      **{f"{V} {n}": 100 * x for V, vv in ve.items() for n, x in zip(("null", "pot", "both"), vv)}))
seed_df = pd.DataFrame(seed_rows)
srows = []

Result (fig4c-alm-null-potent-similar): partially reproduced, resting on reading G1. Over the 5 ALM and medulla sessions, the paired t test finds no difference between null and potent variance in ALM under the main reading (V1 51.3 against 79.6%, p = 0.086; V2 23.2 against 36.9%, p = 0.125; V3 70.5 against 87.7%, p = 0.194), nor under W2 or D2, but no reading of M3 to M6 puts both means within tolerance of 36.0 and 37.1%. Under B2 the test finds potent above null (V1 p = 0.040, V2 p = 0.029), with means out of tolerance. The z-score of example.m, a variant in the claims file, puts both V2 means within tolerance (30.2 against 29.0%), and there the test finds a difference (p = 0.028). With 5 sessions the test has little power: the main-reading V1 difference is 28.3 points. Over the five seeds the main-reading V1 p ranges from 0.079 to 0.086, and the B2 V1 p is 0.040. Under reading G2 (second notebook, 19 sessions) the main reading with V2 gives 33.9 against 42.7%, p = 0.251 (0.249 to 0.261 over the seeds), which the criterion counts as reproduced; the outcome here rests on G1, which is held fixed while the readings of M3 to M6 are searched (see the summary).

Result (fig4c-medulla-null-smaller): reproduced under the claim's seed, resting on readings G1, B2 and V2, and sensitive to the seed. Under B2 (supra-threshold runs shorter than 100 ms counted as moving) with V2, the medulla null subspace explains 28.4% and the potent subspace 51.9% (tolerances 26.4 +- 3.9 and 44.8 +- 7.12, so at most 51.92), paired t p = 0.017. Over the five seeds the null mean is 27.9 to 28.8%, the potent mean 51.0 to 52.3% and p 0.017 to 0.024; under two of them the potent mean (52.3%) is just outside tolerance, which makes the claim partially reproduced there. Under the main reading B1 the difference is not significant (V1 54.4 against 67.1%, p = 0.312; V2 34.5 against 41.4%, p = 0.344), nor under W2 or D2; under the example.m z-score V2 gives p = 0.042 with the null mean (31.5%) outside tolerance. B2 also makes the ALM difference significant, so no single reading reproduces both Figure 4c claims. Under reading G2 (19 sessions) null is below potent under the main reading (V2 35.7 against 51.7%, p = 0.027; V1 p = 0.020; V1 and V2 p 0.008 to 0.027 over the seeds) and under B2 (V2 30.8 against 56.4%, p = 0.005), with the null mean outside tolerance in each, which the criterion counts as partially reproduced.

Claim fig4e-medulla-null-lower-dimension¶

The movement-null subspace has lower dimensionality in the medullary reticular nuclei than in ALM (paired t test, p = 7.4e-5).

N1: the shuffle dimension of the stationary activity (before any cap); N2: the participation ratio of the covariance of the movement-null projections. Paired two-sided t test over the ALM and medulla sessions.

Result: not reproduced, resting on reading G1. In the 5 G1 sessions the medulla's movement-null dimensionality is not lower than ALM's under either reading. N1 (shuffle dimension): medulla 7.0, ALM 7.6, p = 0.741, lower in 2 of 5 sessions, and p = 0.68 to 0.741 over the five seeds; W2, B2 and D2 give p = 0.39 to 0.91 (under B2 the medulla is higher, 10.0 against 8.2). N2 (participation ratio): medulla 3.23, ALM 5.27, p = 0.087, lower in 4 of 5; divided by the unit count, p = 0.31. The example.m z-score, a variant, gives N1 medulla 10.2 against ALM 14.4, p = 0.042. Under reading G2 (second notebook, 19 sessions) N1 does not differ (p = 0.98), but N2 is lower in the medulla (3.35 against 5.93, p = 0.027, lower in 14 of 19), which the criterion counts as reproduced; there the medulla N2 is below 1.4 in 5 sessions, each with a unit whose |z| exceeds 3000. The medulla has fewer units than ALM in 2 of the 5 G1 sessions.

Claims fig4d-alm-predicts-medulla-null and fig4d-decoding-asymmetry¶

Ridge (lambda 0.01) from the source's movement-null projections at t and the 8 preceding bins to all target movement-null dimensions at t; 70/30 split of trials; R2 per bin from -1.8 to +1.5 s, averaged (M8). Readings: T1 all trials, T2 correct only; R1 pooled R2, R2 mean over dimensions; predictors standardized or not; A1 mean of both ALM directions, A2 each direction.

In [14]:
bins = np.arange(int(round((ms.TASK_SPAN[0] - ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0]) / ms.BIN)),
                 int(round((ms.TASK_SPAN[1] - ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0]) / ms.BIN)))


def decode(rng, readings, zread="main", keep_bins=False):
    rows = []
    for kind, sess_map, pairs in (("ALM-medulla", alm_med, [("ALM", "medulla"), ("medulla", "ALM")]),
                                  ("ALM-ALM", bilateral, [("right ALM", "left ALM"), ("left ALM", "right ALM")])):
        for p in sess_map:
            v = sessions[p]
            hit = np.array(v["sess"]["trials"]["outcome"])[v["keep"]] == "hit"
            for T in ("T1", "T2"):
                idx = np.arange(len(hit)) if T == "T1" else np.where(hit)[0]
                perm = rng.permutation(idx)
                ntr = int(round(0.7 * len(perm)))
                train, test = perm[:ntr], perm[ntr:]
                for src, tgt in pairs:
                    xs, xt = fits[(p, src, zread)]["proj"], fits[(p, tgt, zread)]["proj"]
                    for stdz, pooled in readings:
                        r2, r2_span = ms.ridge_r2(xs, xt, train, test, bins, stdz, pooled, span=True)
                        rows.append(dict(kind=kind, session=p, T=T, src=src, tgt=tgt,
                                         std=stdz, R="R1" if pooled else "R2", r2=100 * r2.mean(),
                                         r2_span=100 * r2_span, r2_median=100 * np.median(r2),
                                         d_src=xs.shape[2], d_tgt=xt.shape[2], n_train=len(train),
                                         **({"r2_bins": r2, "tgt_var": xt[test][:, bins].var(0).mean(1)} if keep_bins else {})))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


ALL_READ = [(s_, p_) for s_ in (False, True) for p_ in (True, False)]
dec_main = decode(np.random.default_rng(seed("fig4d-alm-predicts-medulla-null")), ALL_READ, keep_bins=True)


def dec_summary(df, col="r2"):
    df = df.assign(r2=df[col])
    out = []
    for (T, stdz, R), d in df.groupby(["T", "std", "R"]):
        am_ = d[(d.kind == "ALM-medulla") & (d.src == "ALM")].set_index("session").r2
        ma_ = d[(d.kind == "ALM-medulla") & (d.src == "medulla")].set_index("session").r2
        aa = d[d.kind == "ALM-ALM"]
        a1 = aa.groupby("session").r2.mean()
        rl = aa[aa.src == "right ALM"].r2
        lr = aa[aa.src == "left ALM"].r2
        sem = lambda x: x.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(x))
        t, pv = stats.ttest_rel(am_.loc[ma_.index], ma_)
        out.append(dict(T=T, std=stdz, R=R, ALM_to_med=am_.mean(), sem1=sem(am_), med_to_ALM=ma_.mean(),
                        sem2=sem(ma_), p_asym=pv, ALM_ALM_A1=a1.mean(), sem3=sem(a1), R_to_L=rl.mean(),
                        L_to_R=lr.mean()))
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

Readings of the R2 and of the z-score, and where the negative values come from. The same splits (claim seed) under: R2 over the whole span (residuals summed over bins, over the variance of the test targets about their mean over all bins and trials, which keeps the time-locked variance that the per-bin R2 removes; not in the claims file's M8, a variant); the median over bins next to the mean; and the subspaces of the example.m z-score (claims, M3 variant), whose rates have lighter tails. Then, per session, the per-bin R2 by epoch and the across-trial variance of the test targets at each bin (T1, unstandardized, R1, main reading).

zmax = {(p, r): f["z_absmax"] if "z_absmax" in f else float(np.abs(f["z"]).max())
        for (p, r, rn), f in fits.items() if rn == "main"}
zmax_all = {(p, r): f["z_absmax"] for (p, r, rn), f in fits.items() if rn == "Zall" and "z_absmax" in f}
print("largest |z| over regions: baseline z-score %.0f to %.0f; example.m z-score (bilateral) %.0f to %.0f"
      % (min(zmax.values()), max(zmax.values()), min(zmax_all.values()), max(zmax_all.values())))

# per-bin R2 by epoch, main reading, T1, unstandardized, R1
sel = dec_main[(dec_main["T"] == "T1") & (~dec_main["std"]) & (dec_main.R == "R1")]
tb = ms.WINDOWS["W1"][0] + ms.BIN * bins
ep_masks = {"sample": (tb < -1.2), "delay": (tb >= -1.2) & (tb < 0), "response": tb >= 0}
brows = []
for _, r in sel.iterrows():
    row = dict(kind=r.kind, session=r.session.split("/")[1][:30], src=r.src, z_absmax_src=round(zmax[(r.session, r.src)]),
               predictors_per_train_trial=round(9 * r.d_src / r.n_train, 2), r2_mean=round(r.r2, 1), r2_median=round(r.r2_median, 1),
               bins_below_minus1=round(float(np.mean(r.r2_bins < -1)), 2), worst_bin=round(100 * float(r.r2_bins.min())))
    for ep, m in ep_masks.items():
        row[f"R2 {ep}"] = round(100 * float(r.r2_bins[m].mean()), 1)
        row[f"var {ep}"] = round(float(r.tgt_var[m].mean()), 3)
    brows.append(row)
bin_df = pd.DataFrame(brows)
print(bin_df.to_string())
print("across sessions and directions, Spearman correlation of mean R2 with the source's largest |z|: %.2f, "
      "with the predictors per training trial: %.2f"
      % (stats.spearmanr(bin_df.r2_mean, bin_df.z_absmax_src).correlation,
         stats.spearmanr(bin_df.r2_mean, bin_df.predictors_per_train_trial).correlation))
allr = dec_main[(dec_main["T"] == "T1") & (~dec_main["std"]) & (dec_main.R == "R1")].assign(ppt=lambda d: 9 * d.d_src / d.n_train)
print("all sessions and directions (incl. ALM to ALM), Spearman correlation of mean R2 with predictors per training trial: %.2f; "
      "R2 above 0 in %d of %d, whose largest predictors per trial is %.2f"
      % (stats.spearmanr(allr.r2, allr.ppt).correlation, (allr.r2 > 0).sum(), len(allr),
         allr[allr.r2 > 0].ppt.max() if (allr.r2 > 0).any() else np.nan))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.2))
for _, r in sel[sel.kind == "ALM-medulla"].iterrows():
    ax[0].plot(tb, 100 * np.clip(r.r2_bins, -5, 1), lw=0.6, label=f"{r.session.split('_')[1][4:12]} {r.src}")
    ax[1].plot(tb, r.tgt_var, lw=0.6)
ax[0].set(xlabel="time from go cue (s)", ylabel="R2 (%), clipped at -500", title="per-bin R2, ALM and medulla sessions")
ax[1].set(xlabel="time from go cue (s)", ylabel="across-trial variance of target", yscale="log", title="test targets")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=5)
plt.tight_layout()
print("per-bin R2 below -500%% (clipped in the plot): %d of %d bins"
      % (sum(int((r.r2_bins < -5).sum()) for _, r in sel[sel.kind == "ALM-medulla"].iterrows()), len(bins) * (sel.kind == "ALM-medulla").sum()))
print("elapsed %.0f s" % (time.time() - T0))

Result (fig4d-alm-predicts-medulla-null): not reproduced. With lambda = 0.01 the decoder fails on held-out trials under every reading: mean R2 from -611.5 to -249.1% for ALM to medulla and from -6098.6 to -2191.3% for ALM to ALM (A1), against 40 and 54%, and it stays negative under the five seeds. The negative values are not an artefact of the averaging or the denominator: the median over bins is -364.9 to -178.8% (ALM to medulla), and the R2 over the whole span, which keeps the time-locked variance, is -320.8 to -120.3%. Nor do they come mainly from the heavy tails of the baseline z-score: with the example.m z-score, whose largest |z| is 24 to 124 in the bilateral sessions, ALM to medulla falls to -1828.9 to -1512.9%. Over the 44 session and direction pairs the R2 falls with the number of predictors per training trial (9 times the source dimensions over the training trials; Spearman correlation -0.61) more than with the source's largest |z| (-0.24); it is above zero in 3 of 44 pairs, all with 0.24 predictors per trial or fewer. The nine lagged copies of the smoothed projections are nearly collinear (condition number about 1e6), and lambda = 0.01 barely regularizes them. In the variants with larger penalties R2 is at most 16.6% (ALM to medulla, lambda 100), and ALM to ALM (6.9%) stays below ALM to medulla, the reverse of the paper.

Result (fig4d-decoding-asymmetry): not reproduced. Under every reading the paired t test of ALM to medulla against medulla to ALM gives p = 0.70 to 0.99 over the 5 sessions, and medulla to ALM R2 is -517.9 to -290.4%, against 21 +- 6.7%; over the five seeds p is 0.45 to 1.00. Under the median over bins, the R2 over the span and the example.m z-score, p is 0.11 to 0.99. In the lambda = 100 variant ALM to medulla exceeds medulla to ALM by 6.2 points (p = 0.091), with medulla to ALM at 10.4%. Under reading G2 (second notebook) every R2 is below -10^6 % and p is 0.15 to 0.87.

Claim fig4f-medulla-null-not-spanning-alm¶

In a joint UMAP embedding of movement-null activity, medullary units do not span the set of movement-null activity patterns seen in ALM.

M10: equal numbers of left and right correct trials, half to train and half to test; trial-averaged movement-null reconstructions (X Q Q') of both trial types concatenated in time; z-scored per unit on the training set; UMAP (2 components, 30 neighbours, min_dist 0.3, cosine), fitted on the training data of ALM and medulla units together, test data transformed. The paper judges by inspection; the numbers below describe the test embedding: for each unit, whether any of its 10 nearest neighbours is from the other region, against the same count with the region labels shuffled (1000 times) over all units and within each session (which keeps any clumping of units by session). The embedding is also shown by session, with each region's extent, and again without the session whose medulla has a one-dimensional null subspace.

import umap
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors


def umap_run(rng, random_state, exclude=()):
    train_rows, test_rows, region, sess = [], [], [], []
    for p, s in alm_med.items():
        if p in exclude:
            continue
        v = sessions[p]
        trials = v["sess"]["trials"]
        out_arr = np.array(trials["outcome"])[v["keep"]]
        instr = np.array(trials["trial_instruction"])[v["keep"]]
        r_idx = rng.permutation(np.where((out_arr == "hit") & (instr == "right"))[0])
        l_idx = rng.permutation(np.where((out_arr == "hit") & (instr == "left"))[0])
        n = min(len(r_idx), len(l_idx))
        r_idx, l_idx = r_idx[:n], l_idx[:n]
        h = n // 2
        for reg in ("ALM", "medulla"):
            f0 = fits[(p, reg, "main")]
            rec = f0["z"] @ f0["qn"] @ f0["qn"].T
            tr = np.concatenate([rec[r_idx[:h]].mean(0), rec[l_idx[:h]].mean(0)], axis=0)
            te = np.concatenate([rec[r_idx[h:]].mean(0), rec[l_idx[h:]].mean(0)], axis=0)
            mu, sd = tr.mean(0), tr.std(0)
            sd = np.where(sd > 0, sd, 1.0)
            train_rows.append(((tr - mu) / sd).T)
            test_rows.append(((te - mu) / sd).T)
            region += [reg] * tr.shape[1]
            sess += [p.split("/")[1][:30]] * tr.shape[1]
    Xtr, Xte = np.vstack(train_rows), np.vstack(test_rows)
    model = umap.UMAP(n_components=2, n_neighbors=30, min_dist=0.3, metric="cosine", random_state=random_state)
    model.fit(Xtr)
    return model.transform(Xte), np.array(region), np.array(sess)


def nn_stats(emb, region, rng, k=10, n_shuffle=1000, within=None):
    """Observed shares, and the null with region labels shuffled over all units or, with `within`
    (a session label per unit), within each session."""
    nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=k + 1).fit(emb)
    _, ind = nn.kneighbors(emb)
    ind = ind[:, 1:]

    def frac(lab):
        other = lab[ind] != lab[:, None]
        alm_alone = np.mean(~other[lab == "ALM"].any(1))
        med_with_alm = np.mean(other[lab == "medulla"].any(1))
        return alm_alone, med_with_alm

    def shuffled():
        if within is None:
            return rng.permutation(region)
        lab = region.copy()
        for s_ in np.unique(within):
            m = within == s_
            lab[m] = rng.permutation(region[m])
        return lab

    obs = frac(region)
    null = np.array([frac(shuffled()) for _ in range(n_shuffle)])
    return obs, null


umap_res = {}
for k in SEED_OFFSETS:
    sd_ = seed("fig4f-medulla-null-not-spanning-alm", k)
    rng_u = np.random.default_rng(sd_)
    emb, region, sess = umap_run(rng_u, random_state=sd_ % (2 ** 31))
    obs, null = nn_stats(emb, region, rng_u)
    _, null_w = nn_stats(emb, region, rng_u, within=sess)
    umap_res[k] = (emb, region, sess, obs, null, null_w)
    print(f"seed offset {k}: ALM units with no medulla unit among 10 neighbours {100 * obs[0]:.1f}% "
          f"(labels shuffled over all units {100 * null[:, 0].mean():.1f}%, within session {100 * null_w[:, 0].mean():.1f}%, "
          f"95th pct {100 * np.percentile(null_w[:, 0], 95):.1f}%); "
          f"medulla units with an ALM neighbour {100 * obs[1]:.1f}% (over all {100 * null[:, 1].mean():.1f}%, "
          f"within session {100 * null_w[:, 1].mean():.1f}%, 5th pct {100 * np.percentile(null_w[:, 1], 5):.1f}%)")
emb, region, sess, obs, null, null_w = umap_res[0]

Result: partially reproduced. In the test-set embedding 25.7% of ALM units have no medulla unit among their 10 nearest neighbours, against 0.1% with the region labels shuffled over all units and 0.1% with them shuffled within each session (21.3 to 27.3% over the five seeds), and 6 of the 26 grid cells that hold ALM units hold no medulla unit. So part of the ALM movement-null patterns has no medulla counterpart, as the paper reports, and this is not the clumping of units by session, which the within-session shuffle keeps. The second part of the criterion holds only in part. On the grid of the claim seed's embedding no medulla cell (0 of 20) lies outside the cells that hold ALM units, but only 59.4% of medulla units have an ALM unit among their neighbours (99.7% with labels shuffled within session; 58.2 to 62.6% over the seeds). The medulla of sub-460436_ses-20200109 has d_null = 1, and its units spread along one line (spread 9.75, against 2.3 to 4.7 for the other regions); without that session (claim seed plus 1), 21.0% of ALM units have no medulla neighbour, 16 of 57 ALM cells hold no medulla unit, and 26 of 67 medulla cells lie outside the ALM cells. The judgment rests on these counts and the plots, as the paper's rests on inspection.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's:

  • Under reading G1 of 'good' the selection gives 5 ALM and medulla sessions (paper 16 or 11) and 17 bilateral sessions (paper 20), so every Figure 4 test here runs on fewer sessions and units than the paper's. Reading G2 (second notebook) gives 19 ALM and medulla sessions with about 2.5 times the paper's units; its CCF labels are transferred from the nearest unit classified good.
  • The movement threshold is Otsu's threshold on the log speed, where the paper set it by hand; the keypoint positions are smoothed (3 frames) first.
  • Ignore, photostimulation and early-lick trials are left out, and so are trials whose delay is not 1.2 s (446 correct and error trials over the 22 sessions).
  • The dimension shuffle uses 100 shuffles on every 4th bin (the paper 1000 on all bins).
  • UMAP runs in umap-learn, not MATLAB's run_umap.
  • The readings of the claims file were each run with the others held at the main reading, not in every combination.
  • The unit selection is held at reading G1 for every outcome, while the readings of M3 to M6 (and the seeds) are searched for one under which a claim holds. fig4c-medulla-null-smaller is reproduced under one such combination (B2 with V2). Applied the same way to G2, fig4c-alm-null-potent-similar would be reproduced (main reading, V2, 33.9 against 42.7%, p = 0.251) and fig4e-medulla-null-lower-dimension reproduced under N2 (p = 0.027). G1 is kept because its bilateral unit counts are near the paper's and its CCF labels are the dataset's own; G2 brings units with a baseline |z| up to 53615 and transferred labels.
  • The numbers depend slightly on the processor that runs the notebook: the linear algebra library picks its kernels by processor, and the last digits of the subspace fits differ between kernels. Most numbers move in the third or fourth digit, but the shuffle dimension of a few G2 regions, the decoding R2 (lambda = 0.01 barely regularizes nearly collinear predictors) and the UMAP embedding amplify the difference. An earlier execution on another runner gave other values for these (listed in the attempt record), with the same outcomes. The text here is written from this execution.

What was found about the dataset:

  • anno_name (the CCF label) is filled only for units whose classification is good (69453 of 272227 units), and 1852 units have no classification. The electrodes table holds CCF coordinates, from which the label of other units can be estimated.
  • The trial table has no column for the delay duration. In the ALM and medulla sessions and the 2021 bilateral sessions, 13 to 57 correct and error trials per session have a 1.8 s or 0.3 s delay, which shows only in the sample and delay event times.
  • Some units have near-silent baselines, so the baseline z-score of the Methods gives values up to 278 s.d. among G1 units and above 50000 among G2 units.
  • The jaw and nose tracking are in pixels, at about 294 Hz, in one segment per trial; unsmoothed, their frame-to-frame jitter hides movement. Nearly every bin of the kept trials has tracking.
  • Clocks: in every selected session the tongue becomes visible a median 56 to 262 ms after the go cue, and lick direction is decoded from spike counts after the go cue above the shuffled labels, so the spike, video and trial clocks are consistent.
  • The units of the session compared are identical in versions 0.230822.0128 and 0.231012.2129.
